info.title: Ruvee API
info.description:
Endpoints that are implemented today, and nothing else. The endpoints proposed in
docs/architecture/api-design.md are not part of this document until they are built.

Authentication is OPAQUE (`/api/v1/auth/*`), followed by a cookie session
(`__Host-ruvee_session`; `ruvee_session` on loopback HTTP development). Every
non-GET `/api/v1` request must send `Origin` equal to the configured public origin and
`x-ruvee-request: 1`, otherwise `403 csrf_rejected`. A bearer token is
not accepted yet. Each operation's `x-ruvee-access` names its level: none, session (pending or
active device), active (enrolled device) or step-up.

Conventions that apply to every request:

- Every response carries `x-request-id`. A caller-supplied value matching
  `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$` is echoed back; any other
  value is replaced by a generated UUID.
- Every response carries `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- Request bodies are read only for POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE. They must be `application/json`
  (UTF-8, no content encoding) and at most 65536 bytes
  (4194304 for `POST /api/v1/sync/commits`). Request schemas reject unknown
  fields.
- Errors use the `ErrorResponse` shape with a code from a closed list and a fixed message.
  Unknown paths return `404 not_found`.
